cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Your Turn
cards.instruction: Get someone to accept responsibility for a task you believe should never have been yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I took your bins out once during your holiday. I didn't volunteer for life. Tonight's yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The neighbours already send you the reminders.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I'll introduce you in the group as their permanent bin contact.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Stay in it until I know what I'm doing?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll stay until you send 'I'll handle Thursday.' They can welcome you while I leave.

mechanism: A presides over the end of an accidental duty, approving temporary support only until B publicly accepts permanent responsibility.
confusable: General delegation could assign any task; D29 needs A belief the duty should not have become theirs, made explicit by the one-time holiday favor.
comparison: Public group commitment replaces private skill training in the bathroom alternative.
seedUse: The existing D29-b exit condition already grants B support request on terms that transfer the responsibility, preserving a workable combined exchange.
